practice.foundation[2]: The booklet does not ask students to select a picture graph from a stated desired symbol key. Constructing a prescribed pictogram and deriving a missing key are different tasks.

practice.foundation[3]: Selecting an interval size from a largest count is not an explicitly asked booklet type. The line-graph scaffold in image46 asks for the axis variables and upper limit, not a comparison of interval sizes.

practice.foundation[4]: The booklet asks students to construct time graphs, but does not separately ask how to order months. This extracts an intermediate construction step rather than an actual source question.

practice.foundation[5]: The question does not specify a column graph, so its solution unnecessarily excludes a valid horizontal bar graph. Assigning categorical graph axes alone is not an explicitly asked source type; image46 asks axes for a prescribed line graph.
practice.development[0]: Choosing the display is source-supported, but the additional stand-alone vertical-scale selection is not an explicitly asked source part for categorical counts.

practice.development[1]: The booklet supports choosing a time display and separately completing a prescribed line-graph axis scaffold, but does not ask this combined display-and-interval-selection task.

practice.development[2]: Evaluating a proposed key using divisibility is not an explicitly asked booklet type. Missing-key questions require deriving the key from a supplied pictogram, which this item does not supply.
practice.development[3]: Comparing proposed numerical interval sizes is not an explicitly asked source type.
practice.development[4]: Choosing a time display is source-supported, but separately requesting the horizontal arrangement extracts a construction step that the booklet does not ask as a question.
practice.development[5]: The graph-choice component is source-supported, but the added numerical-scale selection is not an explicitly asked categorical-data source part.

practice.mastery[0]: Selecting and justifying a pair of scales together with a display is not an explicitly asked booklet type. The solution also omits the requested justification of the vertical scale.
practice.mastery[1]: The display choice is source-supported, but the added stand-alone categorical scale selection is not an explicitly asked source part.

practice.mastery[2]: Critiquing this proposed key and choosing a replacement display with a numerical scale combines demands not explicitly asked in the source. Its structure slug also describes key selection rather than the full critique-and-replacement task.
quiz.q3: Choosing a convenient key from counts alone is not an explicitly asked booklet type. The source's key-selection questions supply a pictogram whose key must be inferred.
quiz.q4: Selecting among numerical vertical-scale plans for categorical counts is not an explicitly asked booklet type.

quiz.q5: Assigning axes for categorical counts alone is not an explicitly asked source type. Specify a column graph if retaining its axis claim, since horizontal bar graphs place categories vertically.
quiz.q6: The combined display, horizontal arrangement and numerical-scale selection is not an explicitly asked booklet type; it bundles construction steps with graph choice.

theory: The decision procedure incorrectly reduces graph choice to categories versus change over time. Include the purpose distinctions taught in the source: comparing quantities, showing proportions of a whole, and showing a numerical distribution, with the corresponding suitable displays; identify the data type as well as the purpose.
summary: Repaired supported graph-choice items by removing unsupported scale and arrangement demands, and replaced unsupported tasks with cited booklet types while retaining all quiz ids and tier sizes. Updated the theory to distinguish data type and purpose, including quantity comparisons, change over time, proportions and numerical distributions; no whole items were removed.
reviewSummary: All 21 items have correct answers, assess the target skill and adapt question types explicitly asked in the Stage 4 booklet; every quiz has exactly one correct option with valid distractor explanations.
